biothings.name: bronchiolitis
biothings.definition: Inflammation of the bronchioles characterized by swelling of the bronchioles and mucus accumulation. It is usually caused by the respiratory syncytial virus and affects children. Signs and symptoms include coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath. [NCIT:P378]

biothings.name: bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome
biothings.definition: A lung disorder that is mainly associated with chronic allograft dysfunction after lung transplantation and that is characterized by inflammation and fibrosis of bronchiolar walls that reduce the diameter of the bronchioles and result in progressive and irreversible airflow obstruction. [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5208-3432, Orphanet:1303]
biothings.synonyms: BOOP, constrictive bronchiolitis, organised pneumonia, organized pneumonia

biothings.name: toxic bronchiolitis
biothings.definition: Bronchiolitis as a response to a toxic exposure. [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

biothings.name: respiratory syncytial virus bronchiolitis
biothings.definition: Bronciolitis caused by infection with respiratory syncytial virus. [MONDO:patterns/infectious_disease_by_agent, PMID:28722988]

biothings.name: postinfectious bronchiolitis obliterans
biothings.definition: An irreversible obstructive lung disease characterized by subepithelial inflammation and fibrotic narrowing of the bronchioles after lower respiratory tract infection during childhood, especially early childhood. Although diagnosis of PIBO should be confirmed by histopathology, it is generally based on history and clinical findings. Irreversible airway obstruction is demonstrated by decreased forced expiratory volume in 1 second with an absent bronchodilator response, and by mosaic perfusion, air trapping, and/or bronchiectasis on computed tomography images. However, lung function tests using spirometry are not feasible in young children, and most cases of PIBO develop during early childhood. [PMID:26770220]

opentargets.name: cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
opentargets.description: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP) is a form of idiopathic interstitial pneumonia characterized pathologically by organizing pneumonia (OP) that presents with non-specific flu-like symptoms, as well as cough and dyspnea and where no etiological agent is found.
